title: Russia Launches Massive Attack on Kyiv — 600 Shahed Drones + 90 Missiles; 4 Killed, 80+ Injured; Every City District Hit
detail: Overnight into May 24, 2026 (Day 1,550 of Russia's full-scale invasion), Russia launched one of the war's largest attacks on Kyiv: approximately 600 Shahed-type loitering munitions and 90 missiles in a sustained overnight barrage. Ukrainian air defense intercepted most drones and more than half the missiles, but a significant number of projectiles penetrated Kyiv's defenses. At least 4 people were killed and more than 80 injured across the city. Damage was recorded in every district of Kyiv, including Obolonskyi, Shevchenkivskyi, Dniprovskyi, Holosiivskyi, Solomianskyi, and Pecherskyi. At least 7 multi-story residential buildings were damaged. The attack came in retaliation for Ukraine's May 22 drone strike on the Starobilsk college dormitory (used as Russian troop billets) that killed 21 and wounded 42. Putin had personally ordered retaliation after calling the Starobilsk strike a 'monstrous crime.' The scale of the May 24 attack — combining Shahed swarm tactics with mass missile salvos — represented a major escalation in Russia's campaign to terrorize the Ukrainian capital. The Russian General Staff claimed targeting of Ukrainian military infrastructure, but civilian casualties and damage to residential areas across all Kyiv districts demonstrated the indiscriminate nature of the bombardment.

title: Russia Fires Oreshnik Hypersonic Ballistic Missile at Bila Tserkva — Third Wartime Use of Nuclear-Capable Weapon
detail: As part of the May 24, 2026 mass attack on Ukraine, Russia fired an RS-26 Rubizh 'Oreshnik' intermediate-range ballistic missile from the Kapustin Yar test range in Astrakhan Oblast, targeting Bila Tserkva in Kyiv Oblast, approximately 50 km south of the capital. This was the third wartime use of the Oreshnik in the war: it was first used against Dnipro on November 21, 2024; second against infrastructure in Lviv Oblast on January 9, 2026; and now against Bila Tserkva on May 24, 2026. The Oreshnik features multiple independently targetable re-entry vehicles (MIRVs), reaching speeds of up to Mach 10-13 that make it nearly impossible to intercept with current Ukrainian air defenses. The missile is nuclear-capable, and Russia's use of it carries deliberate strategic signaling value — threatening nuclear escalation while delivering conventional warheads. President Zelensky confirmed the Oreshnik use in a formal statement. The deployment of an intermediate-range nuclear-capable ballistic missile against a city 50 km from Ukraine's capital represented a significant escalation in Russia's efforts to terrorize the Ukrainian civilian population and signal to Western partners the limits of their involvement.

media.caption: Russia fires Oreshnik hypersonic ballistic missile at Bila Tserkva (50 km south of Kyiv) — 3rd wartime use of nuclear-capable weapon (May 24, 2026)

title: Ukrainian General Staff: 1,110 Russian Soldiers Killed or Wounded in Past 24 Hours — Cumulative Losses Reach ~1,355,920
detail: Ukraine's General Staff reported on May 24, 2026 that approximately 1,110 Russian soldiers were killed and wounded in the past 24 hours — a sharp spike from the 950 reported on May 23 — reflecting the intense combat activity across the front on May 23. Cumulative Russian military personnel losses since February 24, 2022 reached approximately 1,355,920. Equipment destroyed since the invasion: 11,950 tanks, 24,603 armored fighting vehicles, 42,640 artillery systems, 436 aircraft, 353 helicopters, and 308,321 UAVs. The daily loss spike to 1,110 is among the highest recorded in 2026. The sustained high Russian casualty rates — averaging 1,000+ daily in 2026 — have prompted Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief Syrskyi to assess that Russia faces a deepening recruitment crisis that has allowed Ukraine to seize the tactical initiative for the first time in the full-scale war.
